study: Jerrim et al. 2015 — EEF Mathematics Mastery (Secondary), delivered by Ark; UCL IoE evaluation
eval_evidence: EEF/DfE-funded efficacy trial independently evaluated by UCL Institute of Education; Ark (the developer/delivery charity) recruited schools and delivered the programme but did not conduct the impact evaluation.
developer_evidence: Mathematics Mastery was 'initially developed by Ark Schools' and the programme 'was delivered by the education charity Ark' — the developer organisation delivered the training and support directly.
cascade_evidence: Ark delivered 1-2 days of launch training, in-school development visits, and multi-school cluster workshops directly to headteachers, maths coordinators and class teachers; no train-the-trainer intermediary layer.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'proceed with business as usual' during 2013/14; eligible to access MM only after the trial. No alternative PD/program for controls.
coaching_evidence: Support model = 1-2 launch training days + TWO in-school development visits + three multi-school cluster workshops + online CPD toolkit across the year. Two periodic in-school visits = light/periodic support, not recurring monthly in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Whole-class 'mastery' maths curriculum/pedagogy delivered by the Year 7 maths teacher in normal lessons; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Report explicitly notes 'this was the first year the programme had been introduced'; outcomes measured at end of that first implementation year (summer 2014). Teachers new to MM.
